rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The KCNQ1 gene encodes a potassium channel subunit critical for cardiac repolarization. Mutations in this gene are known to cause long QT syndrome and other arrhythmogenic conditions. Atrial fibrillation in patients with KCNQ1 mutations often has a strong genetic component, but environmental triggers like alcohol, stress, or sleep deprivation can precipitate episodes. The combination of genetic predisposition and environmental factors explains the observed link in this case.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: KCNQ1 mutations are well-documented to cause arrhythmias including atrial fibrillation, with environmental factors exacerbating the condition.
